checkpoints.description: [1/2] Pre-register and implement the HO-2 radial-shell finite-core probe in Rust with failing-first unit tests and independent audit rows

impact_assessment.benefits: Advances the defect-core program on the sole Rust main implementation, distinguishes radial shells from quantized vortices, and adds independently re-derived G-001 evidence rather than another representation-only identity.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use u=rR so u''/u equals the full s-wave radial Laplacian ratio; freeze eps0=0.1a0, physical grids and analytic phase/Q/norm gates in ADR-058 before seeing results; add compile-failing tests first; independently re-derive the gates in audit.rs and verify in two processes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new fluid checks and audit rows change fingerprints/report counts; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: source, tests, ledger, scorecard, changelog and generated reports; physics: an incorrect radial Laplacian or trivial finite-domain phase gate could misclassify the shell.
impact_assessment.why: Claim 61 explicitly queues the hydrogen-2s radial shell; the Rust core currently has only the HO-1 and 2p closed forms, so the next falsifiable gap is whether a single-valued complex-shift 2s core has finite radial velocity and quantum pressure while preserving the singular control and zero m=0 circulation.
